frozen_question: Does changing the mechanical/ECM state of the repair niche causally change regenerative versus scar/containment outcome in at least three independent mammalian tissues, while preserving tissue-specific direction and timing?

counted_strong_tissues.basis: developmental ECM stiffening aligns with rapid postnatal loss of cardiac regenerative competence; experimental ECM softening/fetal-matrix conditions extend regenerative behavior in low-regenerative neonatal heart models
counted_strong_tissues.boundary: does not establish a universal stiffness threshold or direct adult-human regeneration therapy

counted_strong_tissues.basis: mechanical tension/mechanotransduction perturbations alter YAP-linked fibroblast scar trajectories; Huang et al. 2026 additionally couples mechanical buffering to apoptotic-cell clearance and reduced persistent alpha-SMA/fibrotic outcome
counted_strong_tissues.boundary: compound biomaterial/drug interventions and immediate treatment do not identify a delayed safe-resolution window

counted_strong_tissues.basis: AFM shows age-associated spinal-cord stiffening and marked lesion stiffening; neonatal-like mechanical retuning of an adult SCI lesion changes axon regrowth, circuit-associated histology and functional recovery; an independent stiffness-varied scaffold study replicates causal mechanical sensitivity
counted_strong_tissues.boundary: stiffness is tuned through scaffold formulation, so mechanics are not perfectly isolated from polymer-density/transport/adhesion effects

supportive_not_counted_as_clean_strong.evidence: 2026 stiff-versus-soft PVA-SHMP scaffold study changes alpha-SMA suppression, collagen maturation and functional repair
supportive_not_counted_as_clean_strong.reason_not_counted: mechanics were changed by SHMP concentration, coupling stiffness to network chemistry and degradation; developmental lock causality is not isolated
regenerative competence loss is strongly supported on epigenetic/plasticity axes, but stiffness is not established as the primary causal lock

falsification_controls.finding: a different GelMA model reported greater axonal extension and sensory recovery with the higher-stiffness formulation

falsification_controls.cross_tissue_rule: mechanical effects can reverse sign depending on phase, geometry, absolute modulus, tissue load-bearing role, scaffold architecture and cell identity

gate_decision.best_supported_model: Each tissue has a permissible mechanical niche/state range that changes with development and injury. Moving the niche away from that range can stabilize non-regenerative repair states; experimentally retuning mechanics can change outcome, but the favorable direction and threshold are tissue- and context-specific.
gate_decision.claim_ceiling: Three independent mammalian tissues now support causal importance of mechanical niche state. This is not evidence for one universal modulus, one universal softer-is-better rule, or human regenerative efficacy.

relation_to_resolution_gate.skin: mechanical buffering can improve apoptotic-cell clearance/efferocytosis and reduce persistent fibrotic state
relation_to_resolution_gate.spinal_cord: mechanical retuning improves axonal regeneration but current intervention is immediate and does not measure late scar-cell EXIT
relation_to_resolution_gate.heart: mechanics and fibroblast-state transitions overlap temporally but should remain separate evidence roots unless the same experiment links them

relation_to_exit_clock.reason: the decisive new spinal-cord interventions are applied at injury rather than after structural stabilization; they establish a mechanical-state gate, not a delayed resolution clock

next_killer_gate.name: MECHANICAL_STATE_TIMING_GATE
requirements: at least two tissues with delayed mechanical retuning after the repair state is established
point-level tissue stiffness/force measurements before and after intervention
same-state cellular readouts showing whether mechanical retuning precedes resolution or regenerative re-entry
function/structural outcome showing benefit without destabilizing necessary early repair
highest_value_targets: skin: delayed mechanical buffering after alpha-SMA rise
spinal cord: delayed neonatal-like softening after lesion stiffness/scar is established
heart: delayed ECM/crosslinking or mechanotransduction intervention after infarct stabilization with direct tissue mechanics
